note: Which scanners a run class must measure and which it may leave unmeasured (#763, #764, docs/specs/qualification-adapter.md, 'The scanner roster'). Read by the adapter and the official-run driver. Not a component of the product policy revision: it names who is measured, not what a status requires, so it moves no support status.

openredaction.label: OpenRedaction default (all patterns)
openredaction.reason: The default (all-pattern) profile is slow and noisy for credential evaluation: personal data and resource identifiers dominate its findings, and its last official measurement took 7 minutes of scanner time on a population the credential profile scans in seconds (its methods run takes 40+ minutes), so it is a manual measurement and never blocks other scanners or core verification (#763). Its earlier results stay as history with their run identity; the credential profile is a separate scanner, never spliced with it.
openredaction.detects: Every built-in OpenRedaction pattern (579 in 1.1.5): credentials and also personal data (names, phone numbers, handles) and resource identifiers. Most of its findings are out of scope for credential evaluation.

retainedMeasurements.note: The last official measurement of the default profile: the four canonical linux-x64 runs of the snapshot-2026.10.05 acceptance on credential-eval alpha.5. The repin to alpha.15 (and the four-scanner default) dropped them from official-runs.json, so the roster keeps the pointer; the artifacts are retained in the archive release below and each is checked by its byte digest.

openredaction-credential-bearing.label: OpenRedaction credential profile (33 types)
openredaction-credential-bearing.detects: Only the 33 credential-bearing OpenRedaction pattern types (the credentials category plus URL_WITH_AUTH): API keys and tokens, private keys, connection strings, session identifiers. No personal-data or resource-identifier pattern runs, so it cannot flag or accidentally overlap them.
openredaction-credential-bearing.disclosure: Both are OpenRedaction 1.1.5 under different configurations. The profile scans less, so its results differ from the default's by configuration: it is not a more accurate OpenRedaction, and no accuracy claim is made for either profile.
openredaction-credential-bearing.statement: OpenRedaction credential profile (33 types): not measured in an official run (local exploratory diagnostics only: see ADR)
openredaction-credential-bearing.reason: The credential profile is the comparison profile chosen in docs/decisions/2026-10-06-choose-the-openredaction-credential-bearing-profile-as-the-comparison-scanner.md. It is optional in the official run class because no pinned engine configuration measures it yet: making it required would refuse every official view until the owner approves the one profile-only run. Its own history starts with that run; nothing of the default's is reused for it.
openredaction-credential-bearing.officialMeasurement: pending: requires owner approval (one profile-only run; see the decision)
openredaction-credential-bearing.engineRelease: not needed: the released alpha.12 engine runs the profile from a configuration held in this repository
